clue.text: He's rich, eccentric and fourth in line for county

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written
the fourth letter of line

explanation.surface: A wealthy oddball who stands fourth in the succession to some English county estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' reads as a line of succession, but it only supplies its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is an English county in the north-west, home of the grinning cat and the cheese.

clue.text: Grant delivered dye

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word wanted is the one that matches what is heard

blocks.note: Hugh Grant is the English film actor

explanation.surface: A grant of money has been handed over to pay for dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a gift of money or a verb; it is the actor Hugh Grant, and his first name sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a colour or tint, which is what a dye gives to cloth, so the two stand as loose synonyms.

clue.text: Singer voiced part

blocks.note: Cher is the American pop singer, said 'shair'

explanation.surface: A vocalist sang her part in the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A share is a portion or part of something divided among several people.

clue.text: 999p ÷ @1 causing irritability?

definitions.note: the clue's question mark marks the playful arithmetic, not the definition

indicators.note: the division sign says the item before it is split apart, with the item after it placed in the gap

blocks.note: one less than a thousand in Roman numerals, I before M
p is the abbreviation for pence
the @ symbol is read as the word at
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A baffling sum in symbols, the sort of thing that would make anyone short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: IM is a non-standard but crosswordly way of writing 999. PENCE is divided by AT I: IM + P(ATI)ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless annoyance at delay, which is close in meaning to irritability.

clue.text: Guarantee blame after Conservative loss

explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative loss' reads as an election defeat; it is the letter C going missing from the word for blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain it happens, which is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Ill — will he swallow one capsule to begin with?

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside, so the following items go within the word for he
to begin with points at only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: he refers to a male
Roman numeral one
the first letter of capsule

explanation.surface: Someone poorly wonders whether a patient will take a pill to start the treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits 'Ill' and 'will', which together make the phrase ill will. The rest is MAL(I C)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, which is exactly what the phrase ill will means.

clue.text: Average bloke touring Spain

indicators.note: someone touring a country goes all round it, so one item wraps the other

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap on holiday travelling round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man; M(E)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Idyllic place of contentment for auto enthusiasts?

clue.text: Exaggerated profiles rate a circus 'poor'

taken as written
taken as written

blocks.note: standard abbreviation

clue.text: Name-dropping Star Trek actor takes time with small breaks

explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces, so shatters fits breaks as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Exciting incident as a criminal turned to steal banks from Venice

taken as written
the first and last letters of Venice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the material; 'criminal' does the rearranging, and the bank-robbing picture hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an unusual, exciting or daring experience, an exciting incident in plain words.

clue.text: Tate Modern's 9:23

definitions.note: 23 is the answer to 23 down, march, in its sense of protesting in the street

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are cross-references: 9 across is REVAMP, the anagram signal, and 23 down is MARCH, the definition. Tate Modern is London's modern art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to take part in a public protest march, so the verb march stands for it.

clue.text: Mentally prepare for endless horror film

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter of the film title is dropped

blocks.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 horror classic

explanation.definitionFit: To psych yourself (up) is informal for getting into the right frame of mind before a challenge.

clue.text: Pope's legacy: avoiding prison in retirement, simply

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for prison is read backwards

taken as written
a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: A retired pontiff's legacy was keeping out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' is the papal name, not a man to be housed in the prison; 'in retirement' turns the prison word round before it is removed from the inheritance word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act innocently is to act artlessly or guilelessly, one sense of simply.

clue.text: Derided and cut short after capital doubles?

explanation.definitionFit: To mock is to ridicule or scoff at, so mocked is a past-tense synonym of derided.

clue.text: Fish and tea seller in New York

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' flags an American spelling rather than a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The chavender is an old name for the chub, a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Female, one entering pub with tense baby

clue.text: Subtlety shown by religious person describing a church

taken as written

the present is now

clue.text: Pieces of Cambridge college

clue.text: Difficult actress rejects Oscar, finally

the last letter of Oscar

clue.text: Some tutor moving farthest away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Personally crafted by female attendant discounting one note

clue.text: Express disapproval over end of supper with extremely little soup?

clue.text: Cutting very critical leading actor to be replaced by unknown
